newsitem.title: USA: Cenit asks holders reject Mid-Atlantic plan.
newsitem.headline: Cenit asks holders reject Mid-Atlantic plan.

text.p: Cenit Bancorp Inc said Thursday it urged its shareholders to reject a proxy campaign mounted by the Mid-Alantic Investors group.
The group's scheme, Cenit said in a statement, "would likely devalue the company by forcing a premature merger or sale."
Mid-Alantic, led by investor Jerry Shearer, holds a 9.7 percent stake in Cenit, a $707-million asset thrift holding company for Cenit Bank,

The group has sent Cenit shareholders a proxy card seekig shareholder backing for its plan to nominate three candidates to four directors' seats to be filled at the thrift's annual meeting scheduled on April 23.
Midlantic, based in Columbia, S.C., is also seeking support for its proposal to hire an investment banker to help Cenit find ways to improve shareholder value.
In a letter to its shareholders, Cenit said Mit-Atlantic was "interested only in short-term gains for itself and not in maximizing long-term value for all shareholders.
The Cenit board, it said, believes that placing a price tag on the company will eliminate any benefit that shreholders might realize from Cenit's "excellent" future prospects.
